blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A nightly solve of a 900-project model ends with reason FEASIBLE and limit TIME; objective_value() is 41,200 and dual_bound() is 42,050. What should the report say?

options.text: No plan yet, since a limit stopped the solve before any plan was found
options.says: That is NO_SOLUTION_FOUND. FEASIBLE always comes with a plan, here worth 41,200.

options.text: The best plan, worth 42,050, since the dual bound is the plan's value
options.says: The dual bound is a value no plan can beat, not a plan; the plan found is worth 41,200.

options.text: The best plan, worth 41,200, since FEASIBLE means every row is kept
options.says: Every row is kept, but FEASIBLE means a limit stopped the search before the plan was proven best.

options.text: A plan worth 41,200, up to 850 below the best, stopped by a limit
options.says: Right: the plan is usable, the gap to the dual bound is 850, and the limit says why the search stopped.

origin.section: The Plan Is the First Solution, and objective_value Raises When There Is None

questions.stem: A service calls result.objective_value() straight after solving and crashes with `ValueError: No primal feasible solution available.` Which ending explains the crash?

options.text: OPTIMAL within a gap tolerance, since such a plan's value is not stored
options.says: OPTIMAL always carries a plan, gap tolerance or not; objective_value() reads it.

options.text: INFEASIBLE, since no plan keeps every row, so there is no value to read
options.says: Right: an infeasible model has no primal solution, and objective_value() raises ValueError. Check the reason first.

options.text: FEASIBLE, since a limit stopped it and the value waits for a proof
options.says: FEASIBLE is guaranteed to carry a plan, and objective_value() returns its value.

options.text: UNBOUNDED from HiGHS, since its result carries no feasible point
options.says: The lesson's HiGHS UNBOUNDED result carried a point with value 0.0; objective_value() did not raise.

origin.section: The Plan Is the First Solution, and objective_value Raises When There Is None

questions.stem: Finance asks for the shadow price of `budget_2030` after the yes/no selection model is solved with HiGHS. What does `result.dual_values(budget_2030)` do?

options.text: Returns the root LP's price, since HiGHS always solves that LP first
options.says: The result of a MILP solve carries no dual solution at all, root LP or not; the call raises.

options.text: Returns a price per $k, since the row is at its upper bound in the plan
options.says: Whether the row is tight does not matter: the MILP result has no dual solution, and the call raises ValueError.

options.text: Returns 0.0, since an integer plan never fills a budget row exactly
options.says: There is no value to return; has_dual_feasible_solution() is False and dual_values raises.

options.text: Raises ValueError, since a MILP solve returns no dual solution to read
options.says: Right: duals exist for LPs; the lesson's MILP result raised ValueError. Solve the LP relaxation with GLOP or HiGHS for LP prices.

origin.section: Dual Values, Reduced Costs and a Basis Come Only From an LP Solve
